main_text.p: creata ; nec ulla sit omnino potentia hominis impressio in illud quod potestati ipsius subjectum est ; sed tum poten-tia, tum quod sub potentia cadit eveniant potentia Dei. Dicit autem AlKadi AbuBecr facti substantiam evenire potentia Dei, at ut sit factum illud vel obedientia, (ut oratio) vel transgressio (ut scortatio) esse haec epithe-ta, seu conditiones facti quae eveniant potentia hominis: at antistes AlHaramain, (i.e. Mecca & Medina) & Abul-Hafan Basriensis, & sapientes asferunt, facta hominum provenire à potentia quam creavit Deus in homine, & producere Deum in homine potentiam & voluntatem, deinde potentiam & voluntatem istas necessario produce-re quod sub potentia cadit. Praeceptor vero AbulHafan Aspahaniensis dicit illud quod impressionem facit in fa-ctum, esse, potentiam Dei, & potentiam hominis conjun-ctim. Has ubi sententias retulerit, quae contra Al-Motazalos qui hominum actiones libero ipsorum ar-bitrio & potentia permittant, dixerat explica-turus, monet Majores ipsorum cum manifestam ad-verterent differentiam, inter ea quae sub hominum electione cadant,& quae necessario ab inanimatis, in quibus nulla est scientia vel electio,proveniant,atque interim iis urgerentur argumentis quae probant ان الله خالق كل شي Deum omnia creare, seu pro-ducere, ideoque & ea quae ab hominibus fiunt, ut haec inter se conciliarent mediam ingressos viam af-firmasse, الافعال واقعة بقدرة الله تعالي وكسب العبد علي معني ان الله تعالي اجري عادته بان العبد اذا ضدم[?] العزم علي الطاعة ُخالف[?] فعل

page.notes: No marginal notes on this page; the right side is blank. The black ink blots and the "Google" watermark at the lower right are not printed text and are omitted. Doubtful readings: "ضدم" and "خالف" in the last Arabic line (diacritics unclear); "asferunt" as printed; "Aspahaniensis" (printed "Afpahanienfis") and "AbulHafan" as printed. The italic/roman boundary in the Latin is uncertain from line 14 onward; the upper lines are set in italic, and I have marked the Latin of the first thirteen lines as italic, with the rest in roman except "Al-Motazalos" and the gloss "Deum omnia creare". The Arabic words on lines 21–24 are split across the printed lines; I have kept them in the printed order. Catchword "الطاعة" is printed at the foot, right.
